content:
### 🏠 The Mystery of the Missing Pencil

Imagine you are sitting down to draw a beautiful picture of a sun and a tree. You have your paper, your crayons, but... oh no! Your favourite pencil is broken. You need a new one to finish your masterpiece. But you can't find one at home. 

Where will you go to get a new pencil? Will you go to the place where we play on swings? No! Will you go to the place where doctors give medicines? No!

### 🤔 What do you think?

If you want to buy a new pencil, can you go to the hospital? Why not? Where do you think your parents go when they need to buy toys or food for you?

content.title: A Busy Neighbourhood Map
content.description: Look at all the different places around a house!

content:
### 🔍 Discovering Our Surroundings

Think of your house as the center of a big circle. Everything inside that circle is your surroundings. There are many important places around your house that help you and your family every day. There is a place to learn, a place to play, a place to buy things, and a place to get better when you are sick.

### 📖 The Reveal: What is a Neighbourhood?

The area around our house and the places in it make up our **Neighbourhood**. The people who live near our house are our **neighbours**.

Here are some important places in a neighbourhood:
- **Market**: Where we buy food, clothes, and pencils!
- **Hospital**: Where we go when we are sick.
- **School**: Where we go to learn and make friends.
- **Park**: Where we go to play and relax.
- **Post Office**: Where we send letters to our friends and family.

content.definition: The area and places around our house.
A place where sick or injured people are given medical care.
A place where people go to buy and sell things.

content: Some children think that a 'neighbourhood' only means the houses right next to theirs. Remember, a neighbourhood is much bigger! It includes the market, the park, the school, and all the places nearby!

question: Where do we go when we want to buy fruits, vegetables, or a new pencil?
If your friend falls down and gets hurt, which place in the neighbourhood should they visit?

content:
### 💭 Reflection Time

Close your eyes for a minute. Think about the places near your own house. Which is your favourite place to go with your parents? Why do you like it so much? Tell your answer to someone sitting near you!

### 🔗 Making Connections

Did you know that a neighbourhood is like a giant puzzle? Every place is a piece of the puzzle, and every place has special people who help us!

- The School has Teachers.
- The Hospital has Doctors and Nurses.
- The Market has Shopkeepers.

Without these places and these helpers, our puzzle would not be complete!
Encourage the child to look out of the window or take them on a small walk outside. Ask them to point out and name the different places they see in their own neighbourhood.

### 🏆 Mastery Challenge: Become a Map Maker!

Take a blank sheet of paper and some colourful crayons. Draw your house right in the middle of the paper. Now, draw at least 3 places from your neighbourhood around your house (like a park, a school, or a shop). Show your map to your parents and explain what each place is!
